issues.title: Semantic conventions for IAM
issues.body_excerpt:
It should cover the process of authentication (metrics and spans) and define a set of attributes that describe common identities. 

Related: 
https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/issues/1172
https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/issues/1190
https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/issues/2509
https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/issues/3582

This should take into considerations common IAM solutions and work across them. 
This can't be specific to a certain type of identity (human / workload).
This can't be limited to specific domain (GenAI, Cloud).

issues.title: Add Browser Element Timing Event
issues.body_excerpt:
## Change proposal

Add a `browser.element_timing` event describing the render/load timing
metrics reported by the [Element Timing API](https://wicg.github.io/element-timing/)
(`PerformanceElementTiming`), for elements annotated with the
`elementtiming` HTML attribute. Currently supported by Chromium-based
browsers only.

This follows the same pattern as the existing `browser.web_vital` and
`browser.resource_timing` events (#1943).

Proposed body fields: `identifier`, `element`, `render_time`, `load_time`,
`start_time`, `natural_width`, `natural_height`, plus a top-level
`url.full` attribute for the image resource URL.

issues.title: GenAI: silent timeouts are not expressible in agent spans
issues.body_excerpt:
**Area(s):** `area:new` — per template guidance (the dropdown does not list the existing GenAI area). This proposal extends the existing [`docs/gen-ai/gen-ai-agent-spans.md`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/main/docs/gen-ai/gen-ai-agent-spans.md) (+ a note in `gen-ai-exceptions.md`).

---

Hi all — I'd like to open a technical discussion before filing any PR.

**Author context:** I'm the author of [silent-timeout-protocol](https://github.com/chenhz01/silent-timeout-protocol) (MIT/CC-BY-4.0, zero-dependency, stdlib Python) and first raised the underlying failure mode in [langchain-ai/langgraph#9006](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/issues/9006) (26 comments, open). Same handle here, so the authorship trail is continuous.

**The problem in one paragraph.** Current `gen_ai.*` conventions express loud failures well — `error.type`, span `STATUS_ERROR`, exception events. But they are structurally blind to failures that *never emit a signal*: a run that produces no first observable event within its window looks identical to a healthy long-lived span — or to no span at all, when the trigger layer itself is what died; a resumed run whose tool side effects were half-applied carries no marker that reconciliation never happened; a guardrail check that silently did not execute is indistinguishable from one that passed. The most dangerous part of an agent failure is *what didn't happen* — and nothing in the current vocabulary records absence.

**Three concrete shapes** (all live, one with a full capture):

1. **The vanished scheduler layer.** On my own host, an entire morning-automation layer silently disappeared from its scheduler on 2026-10-01: zero active automations, no error, no log record — the trigger layer itself was dead, so nothing downstream could ever report. It was caught only by an external watchdog that checks for the *absence* of expected first signals. Full record: [cases/real-cases.jsonl](https://github.com/chenhz01/silent-timeout-protocol/blob/main/cases/real-cases.jsonl).
2. **Resume after tool timeout** ([langchain-ai/langgraph#9006](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/issues/9006)): a checkpoint-resume proceeds while the timed-out tool's side effects were half-applied — presented downstream as a clean resume.
3. **The absent guardrail check:** fail-closed semantics ("never ran" must count as "denied", never as "pass") are currently inexpressible in span attributes.

issues.title: Make `dns.question.name` opt-in in `dns.lookup.duration` metric
issues.body_excerpt:
### Area(s)

area:dns

### What's missing?

[OBI](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-ebpf-instrumentation) is currently allows to produce the `dns.lookup.duration` as opt-in. we started of following the otel semconv by always adding the `dns.question.name` attribute on the metric. But [we change it to be opt-in](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-ebpf-instrumentation/pull/2088) because of unbounded cardinality issues which causes issues for users.
OBI declares its own telemetry schema that inherits from the otel registry. but if we downgrade the existing requirement level from `required` to `opt-in` that is a breaking change since users will expect that label

### Describe the solution you'd like

Since this metric is still in development and `dns.question.name` does have boundless cardinality i would like to propose to convert it to `opt-in` instead of `required` inside the otel semconv

### Tip

<sub>[React](https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) with 👍 to help prioritize this issue. issues.title: [k8s] Stabilize the metrics used by the kubeletstats receiver
issues.body_excerpt:
Part of https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/issues/3119 (Phase 2).

Following https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/issues/3120, which covered the resource/entity attributes for Phase 1, this issue tracks the **metrics** (and their attributes) that need to be promoted to `release_candidate` so that the [kubeletstats receiver](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/tree/main/receiver/kubeletstatsreceiver) can progress its stability. 

The list below is derived from the receiver's [metadata.yaml](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/blob/main/receiver/kubeletstatsreceiver/metadata.yaml), cross-referenced with [`model/k8s`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/tree/main/model/k8s), [`model/container`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/tree/main/model/container) and the [k8s migration doc](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/main/docs/non-normative/k8s-migration.md) of Semantic Conventions project.

| | count |
| --- | --- |

Nothing under `model/k8s/` or `model/container/` is `stable` at the metric level yet.
